message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's most recent results and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00, which filled at $223.00 for a total of $9,812 — comfortably inside my mandate ($10,000 per order, $20,000 daily cap, buy-only, AAPL/MSFT only, no fund transfers). The limit was set just 0.13% above the $222.70 last trade, so it stayed close to market and filled immediately. The decision rested on verified primary-source figures: Apple's fiscal 2024 fourth quarter (ended September 28, 2024) revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and full-year net sales of $391,035 million, net income of $93,736 million, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating income of $123,216 million, per Apple's newsroom release and its Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR. I noted that FY2024 net income and EPS were slightly below FY2023 ($96,995 million and $6.13) because of a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge, so the underlying operating trend is better than the headline decline suggests. One important caveat: a search result claiming Apple "guided fiscal 2025 EPS to $9.50 with revenue growth above 25%" came from an unfamiliar site and is not credible — Apple doesn't issue annual guidance, and that EPS figure would imply a ~56% jump over the $6.08 just reported — so I excluded it from my reasoning rather than let it inflate the thesis. Sentiment around iPhone 16 demand and the Apple Intelligence rollout appears mixed and roughly neutral, which is consistent with buying a modest position rather than a large one; I have $40,188 in cash remaining and room under the daily cap if a better entry appears.
